title: PrioMQTT: A prioritized version of the MQTT protocol
authors: Gaetano Patti; Luca Leonardi; Giuseppe Testa; Lucia Lo Bello
access: Publisher abstract and metadata; author repository abstract
method: Prioritizes time-critical traffic using a UDP-based MQTT extension.
difference: Transport and protocol intervention; our queue is after delivery. No direct performance comparison is valid without matching the network model.

title: Priority-enabled MQTT: a robust approach to emergency event messaging
authors: P S Akshatha; S Divyashree; S M Dilip Kumar
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science, 71, article 67
method: RabbitMQ virtual queues distinguish urgent, critical and FCFS messages.
difference: Shows that emergency priority queues already exist. We will examine routine waiting and repeated overload rather than claim priority support itself as new.

title: PR-MQTT: a novel approach for traffic reduction and message prioritisation in IoT applications
venue: International Journal of Web Engineering and Technology, 19(1), 44–66
method: Combines selective transmission and urgent-message processing in HBMQTT.
difference: Traffic suppression changes the offered workload; our initial comparisons keep identical input traces. Full text is needed before making absence claims.

title: Towards Integrating MQTT with Time-Sensitive Networking
authors: Giuseppe Testa; Luca Leonardi; Lucia Lo Bello; Gaetano Patti
venue: 2024 IEEE 29th International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
access: Publisher abstract and indexed first-page author text
method: Explores integrating PrioMQTT with TSN for traffic with diverse timing needs.
difference: Network support matters for timing bounds. We make no network-level deadline guarantee from an application queue.

title: Extending MQTT with Real-Time Communication Services Based on SDN
authors: Ehsan Shahri; Paulo Pedreiras; Luis Almeida
access: Full author article in PMC, with publisher DOI
method: Maps application timing requirements to SDN resource reservations.
difference: A broader architecture than our worker queue. Its treatment of ordinary-traffic cost motivates reporting both event classes.

title: Response Time Analysis for RT-MQTT Protocol Grounded on SDN
authors: Ehsan Shahri; Paulo Pedreiras; Luis Almeida
venue: Fourth Workshop on Next Generation Real-Time Embedded Systems (NG-RES 2023), OASIcs 108, 5:1–5:15
access: Publisher abstract and complete bibliographic record
method: Derives worst-case response-time analysis for an SDN-based MQTT architecture.
difference: A formal guarantee requires an explicit analyzable model. Our initial results are empirical finite-workload measurements.

title: Modification of Mosquitto Broker for Delivery of Urgent MQTT Message
authors: Kitae Hwang; Jae Moon Lee; In Hwan Jung; Dong-Hee Lee
venue: 2019 IEEE Eurasia Conference on IOT, Communication and Engineering (ECICE), 166–167
access: Publisher title and indexed first-page author text; bibliographic cross-check in R2
method: Modifies Mosquitto for urgent message delivery.
difference: Prior art for broker-level urgency. Detailed algorithm and evaluation limitations remain unassessed because full text was unavailable.

title: Multi-Tier Message Scheduling for IoT-Based Urban Emergency Systems Through Semantic Priority Override
authors: João Carlos N. Bittencourt; Paulo Portugal; Francisco Vasques; Daniel G. Costa
access: Publisher abstract and metadata; author publication list confirms authors
method: TRIAGE/4 combines semantic alarm priority and device fairness with simulation and an MQTT prototype.
difference: Closest conceptual overlap: alarm latency and fairness are already studied. Any novelty claim needs a full comparison with this method, not just FIFO and strict priority.

title: Real-Time Priority Queue Scheduling for Bursty Traffic
authors: Rongping Lin; Jinpeng Zhang; Shan Luo; Jing Fu; Xiong Wang; Hui Li; Moshe Zukerman
access: University bibliographic record; author postprint method, Algorithm 1 and implementation sections reviewed on 2026-10-21; no independent replication
method: Uses instantaneous switch queue lengths and priorities with a Whittle-index formulation for bursty traffic.
difference: Queue occupancy and priority tradeoffs are prior art. Different switch model; a direct comparison needs explicit model alignment.
